title: fix(rest)!: a schema-derived export skips the fields declared hidden
body:
Fixes #24143

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

**BREAKING** (a served-set narrowing at a REST door): the default columns of `GET /api/v1/data/:object/export` lose every field declared `hidden`. Shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention; the changeset carries the same `Clause-②` line and one ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). This narrowing owes one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record before the queue.

## What changed

- `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`, the export handler's schema-derived column set (no `?fields=`): the column list is `metaMap`'s names minus every field whose definition has `hidden === true`. `metaMap` itself is untouched, so cell formatting and an explicit `?fields=` that names a hidden field are answered as before. The field definitions are read through the existing `templateFieldDefs` (`import-template.ts`), which names fields exactly as `buildFieldMetaMap` does, so no shape normalizer is spelled a third time.
- The route's own doc comment for `fields=`, and one sentence of the `import-template.ts` module header that described the export's default columns, now say what the export does. That header sentence is a comment-only edit outside the dispatched file surface; my change made it false, so it is corrected here rather than left stale.
- Untouched, as ruled: the explicit `?fields=` arm, the FLS narrowing (#3391, #3547) and the headerless no-projection path, `format=json` (it streams rows as the read returns them and has no column set), `?template=true` (its own column rule), and everything in `packages/objectql` and `packages/spec`.

### Shared predicate

None exists. No package exports an "is this field hidden" or "shown by default" predicate: `@objectstack/core` has none, and objectql (`search-companion.ts` `isCompanionSourceEligible`), spec (`field-group-layout.ts`, `record-surface.ts`, `search-fields.ts`) and rest (`form-routes.ts`) each spell `hidden === true` inline. This change spells it the same way, once, at the export's column selection.

## Reach, re-measured on `examples/app-showcase`

A `pnpm dev -- --fresh` boot of this worktree, signed in as the seeded admin. The shipped admin sets carry no `allowExport`, so an environment permission set granting `allowRead` + `allowExport` was saved and assigned to the admin for the measurement. `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task/export?format=csv`, no `fields`:

```text
before (b0fe9fad4): Organization,Created By,Last Modified At,Last Modified By,Owner,Owning Business Unit,Title,Project,Assignee,Status,Priority,Estimate (h),Progress,Done,Due Date,Start Date,End Date,Created,Work Location,Cover,Labels,Notes,Sync Status,Sync Error,Search Index
after  (this PR):   Created By,Last Modified At,Last Modified By,Owner,Title,Project,Assignee,Status,Priority,Estimate (h),Progress,Done,Due Date,Start Date,End Date,Created,Work Location,Cover,Labels,Notes,Sync Status,Sync Error
```

After the fix, `?fields=title,organization_id,__search` still answers the header `Title,Organization,Search Index`, with `Default Organization` in the Organization cells and an empty Search Index.

### Breadth of the narrowing

On the same boot I exported every served object that carries a hidden field: 80 objects, of which 76 answered 200. For each one I compared the header before and after, and counted non-empty cells in each hidden column of the before export. The only labels that left any header are the hidden fields below. No other column moved, and no column appeared.

| hidden field | objects whose default header carried it | value in the before export |
|---|---|---|
| `__search` (Search Index) | 64 | empty on all 190 rows |
| `organization_id` (Organization) | 53 | **carries data**: 167 of 191 rows, the record's organization (`Default Organization` here) |
| `owning_business_unit_id` (Owning Business Unit) | 24 | empty on all 134 rows (nothing stamps it yet, ADR-0117 D2) |
| `sys_session.token` (Session Token) | 1 | empty (the read omits it) |
| `sys_account.previous_password_hashes` | 1 | empty (the read omits it) |
| `sys_api_key.key` (Hashed Key) | 1 | header only, no rows |

No example app (`app-crm`, `app-showcase`, `app-todo`, `app-multi-package`, `embed-objectql`) declares a `hidden` field of its own. The hidden fields are the companion, the two injected scope anchors (`organization_id`, `owning_business_unit_id`), and the three platform-object fields above. `organization_id` is the one column with real data that leaves the default export. A reader who wants it names it in `?fields=`.

## Tests

`packages/rest/src/export-hidden-columns.test.ts` drives the real export route: a real `RestServer` on a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` on a real `ObjectQL`, with a better-sqlite3 `:memory:` driver. The companion is declared by its real producer (`provisionSearchCompanion`), next to an author-declared hidden field that carries a value. The security service answers `getReadableFields` the way plugin-security does for an unrestricted caller: every schema field, the companion included.

- Anti-vacuity: the companion is declared `hidden`, and the readable projection the route asked for admits both hidden fields.
- CSV default, with the security projection: header `ID,Title`; rows unchanged.
- CSV default, without a security service (the masked-row fallback): header `ID,Title`.
- CSV default, zero rows: the projected header is `ID,Title`.
- XLSX default: header row `ID,Title`.
- Control and preservation: explicit `?fields=title,internal_code,__search` answers `Title,Internal Code,Search Index`, with `IC-1`/`IC-2` in the hidden field's cells and an empty companion.

**Ablation**, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor must hit, and restore is checked against the blob). The subject is `data-action-routes.ts`, which the test reaches through relative `./rest-server` imports, so it runs from `src/` and no `dist/` is involved. Mutation: `?.hidden !== true,` became `?.hidden !== 'ablated-24143',`, so the filter keeps every field. The anchor count went from 1 to 0, and the blob went from `7fe336246ce5` to `a690835e24d0`. Result: **4 failed, 2 passed**. All four default pins went red: under the projection the header gained `Internal Code` and `Search Index`, and on the fallback path it gained `Internal Code`. The anti-vacuity case and the explicit-`?fields=` pin stayed green, which shows the explicit arm answers the same with the filter and without it. Restore leg: blob after restore `7fe336246ce5` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

Suite runs (on the merged tree `4f1363cde`):
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: 292 files passed; 6013 tests passed, 326 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: exit 0. The test layer compiles, and `--listFiles` includes the new file.
- `test:repo` for every package whose repo tests can read the changed files (each one scans `packages/` or reads rest's sources): rest (5 files, 254 passed / 12 skipped), core (6 files, 84 passed), spec (66 files, 1105 passed), objectql (1 file, 5 passed) and types (1 file, 11 passed). Runtime's `test:repo` reads only `rest-server.ts` and `meta-item-read-gate.ts` from rest, neither of which this diff touches, so it was not run.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `4f1363cde`: 63 derived commands, all exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation answers 63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the three changed source files: exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- `format=json` has no column projection. It writes each row as the read returns it, so a hidden author field's value stays in a JSON export, and an explicit `?fields=` does not narrow JSON rows either. That was already true before this change. `FieldSchema.hidden` is documented as a UI contract that has never governed serialization, and JSON is the serialization door, so JSON is left as is.
- The import template (`?template=true`) still offers a writable author-declared hidden field as a column (ruling Q2 C on the template). The export and the template now disagree on such a field on purpose: the export answers "what do I see by default", and the template answers "what can I fill".
